stem: The process of starting up a project establishes the prerequisites for initiating a project. Which question is it primarily answering?
answer: Do we have a viable and worthwhile project to initiate?
distractors: How will the project's products be delivered, and by whom?
Is the project still justified now that the stage is complete?
Have the project's benefits been realized and measured?
Should the project be closed early or allowed to continue?
Are the products fit for operational use and ready to hand over?
Which team manager will accept each work package?
explanation: The manual frames the purpose as answering whether a viable and worthwhile project exists, and the process does only the minimum needed to support that judgment. Benefits realization, closure and stage-boundary justification belong to later processes.

stem: Why does PRINCE2 describe starting up a project as a lighter process than initiating a project?
answer: Because it does only the minimum needed to decide whether to initiate
distractors: Because its management products are optional for small projects
Because it is performed entirely outside the project by the business layer, before the manager is appointed
Because it produces no management products of its own
Because the programme supplies everything it would otherwise create
Because it is repeated at every stage boundary rather than done once
Because its activities are carried out after the board authorizes initiation
explanation: The aim is deliberately limited: enough work to judge whether initiation is worthwhile, rather than the detailed and thorough work of initiating a project. The process does produce management products, and it happens before the board is asked to authorize initiation.

stem: Which statement best describes how the process treats poorly conceived project ideas?
answer: It is as much about preventing poorly conceived ideas from being initiated as about progressing viable ones
distractors: It assumes any idea that reaches the mandate has already been justified by the business
It defers the judgment on weak ideas to the first stage boundary, when the board reviews the plan
It initiates every mandated project but limits the resources available to the weak ones
It refers weak ideas to the programme for a benefits review before any work begins, in every case
It treats the mandate as approval to initiate, so weak ideas are filtered during initiation
It requires the project board to reject weak ideas before the executive is appointed
explanation: The process is described as much about prevention as progression, which is why it stays light: only enough is done to judge whether initiation is worthwhile. The decision to start the project is explicit and comes after these activities, so a mandate is not an approval.

stem: Which of these is NOT an objective of the process of starting up a project?
answer: That the project's benefits have been realized and can be measured by the business
distractors: That there is a business justification for initiating the project, documented in an outline business case
That alternative approaches have been evaluated and the chosen project approach agreed
That the work required for the initiation stage is planned in a stage plan
explanation: The objectives cover business justification, the authorities to proceed, enough information to define scope, an agreed project approach, appointed individuals and a planned initiation stage, plus avoiding wasted effort on unsound assumptions. Benefits realization is assessed long after initiation, not as one of its prerequisites.

stem: A project board is told that only one way of delivering the solution was ever considered. Which objective of starting up a project has not been met?
answer: That alternative approaches were evaluated and the chosen approach agreed
distractors: That sufficient information is available to define and confirm the project's scope
That all the necessary authorities exist for initiating the project
That individuals are appointed who will take significant project management roles
That there is a business justification documented in an outline business case
That time is not wasted initiating a project based on unsound assumptions
That the work required for the initiation stage is planned
explanation: One stated objective is that alternative approaches have been evaluated and the chosen project approach agreed, which a single-option analysis does not satisfy. The other options concern justification, authority, scope, appointments or planning, none of which is the gap described.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is the term for whatever information is used to trigger a project?
answer: The project mandate
distractors: The project brief
The project initiation request
The outline business case
The project initiation documentation
The project product description
The business case
explanation: The project mandate is the trigger, whatever form the information takes, such as a feasibility study or a request for proposal. Refining the mandate is what produces the project brief.

stem: What is the minimum the project mandate must contain?
answer: Sufficient information to identify at least the prospective project executive
distractors: An approved business case and a project plan for the initiation stage
A project product description with agreed quality criteria and acceptance methods
Stage tolerances for the initiation stage and the project as a whole
The names of every member of the project board and the project manager
A lessons log and an initial risk register for the project team
A fully costed benefits management approach with review dates
explanation: The mandate should provide the terms of reference and at least enough information to identify the prospective executive of the project board. The other products listed are created during this process or later.

stem: A project is part of a programme. How does that change the work of starting up a project?
answer: The programme should provide the brief and appoint some of the board, and the manager validate it
distractors: The programme provides only the mandate, and the project creates everything else, including the board
The project manager should rebuild the brief independently to avoid inheriting programme assumptions
The process is skipped, because the programme has already justified the project
The programme manager becomes executive and owns the outline business case
The business layer appoints the board and the programme is merely informed
The project brief is replaced by the programme's business case, and the mandate is no longer needed
explanation: Where the project sits inside a programme, the programme management team should supply the brief and appoint board members, which removes much of the work; the project manager validates it and recommends changes if needed. The effort shrinks, but the process is not skipped.

stem: Which two activities does PRINCE2 describe as parallel and iterative, needing frequent consultation between the project manager, board members and other stakeholders?
answer: Preparing the outline business case and assembling the brief
distractors: Assessing previous lessons and selecting the project approach
Appointing the executive and appointing the project manager
Designing the team structure and preparing role descriptions
Planning the initiation stage and requesting project initiation
Creating the daily log and creating the lessons log
Reviewing the mandate and appointing the project management team
explanation: The outline business case and the project brief are built in parallel and iteratively, so effort spent capturing requirements clearly is repaid during initiation and delivery by avoiding issues and replanning. The other pairs are sequential activities or steps inside a single activity.

topic: Appoint the executive and project manager
stem: Which sequence correctly describes the appointments made in the first activity?
answer: The business appoints the project executive, who then appoints the project manager
distractors: The project board appoints the executive, who then appoints the project manager
The business appoints the project manager, who then appoints the executive
The project executive appoints both the project manager and the project board
The project manager appoints the executive, who then appoints the senior user
The programme manager appoints the executive, who then appoints the project board
The business appoints both the executive and the project manager without further involvement
explanation: The business reviews the mandate and appoints the executive, and the executive then identifies, selects and appoints the project manager, possibly needing the business's agreement. The RACI chart confirms the business layer is accountable for this activity and responsible for appointing the executive.

stem: What does the project manager create in the first activity of the process?
answer: The daily log, as a repository for project information and events
distractors: The lessons log, as a record of lessons and associated actions
The project brief, as the basis for the initiation decision
The outline business case, as the justification for the project
The stage plan, as the plan for the initiation stage
The project product description, as the definition of the project's output
The issue register, as the record of issues and changes
explanation: The project manager creates the daily log in this activity as the repository for project information, and risks captured there are reviewed when the outline business case is prepared. The lessons log belongs to the following activity.

stem: In which activity is the lessons log created?
answer: Assess previous lessons
distractors: Appoint the project executive and project manager
Prepare the outline business case
Appoint the project management team
Select the project approach
Assemble the project brief
Plan the initiation stage
explanation: The lessons log is created during assess previous lessons, if appropriate, to record the lessons identified and their associated actions. The daily log, by contrast, is created in the first activity of the process.

stem: Which set of products can lessons from previous projects influence?
answer: The management team design, the outline business case, the brief and the initiation stage plan
distractors: The project mandate, the project board appointments and the project's tolerances
The outline business case and the project brief only, since everything else is planned later
The daily log, the lessons log and the project initiation request, as drafted by the project manager
The stage plan for the first delivery stage and the benefits management approach
The project approach only, because lessons concern delivery methods, and not management products
The quality register, the issue register and the risk register, as created at the start of the stage
explanation: The manual names exactly those four: the team design, the outline business case, the project brief content and the initiation stage plan. Lessons can concern the strengths and weaknesses of processes, techniques and tools, so they reach more of this process's products than the approach alone.

stem: Who develops the outline business case?
answer: The project executive, consulting the senior user if one is appointed
distractors: The project manager, in consultation with the senior supplier and the project board
The business layer, on the project board's behalf
The senior user, in consultation with the project manager and the executive
The project executive acting alone, without consultation
Project assurance, using the project mandate
The programme manager, where the project is part of a programme
explanation: The executive develops the outline business case from the mandate and current knowledge, consulting the senior user if appointed so the contribution to business objectives is understood. The project manager's consultations in this activity produce the project product description, not the business case.

stem: The project manager consults the senior user, senior supplier and project executive to define what the project is to deliver. Which management product is created?
answer: The project product description
distractors: The project brief
The outline business case
The product breakdown structure
The quality management approach
The project plan
The benefits management approach
explanation: Those consultations produce the project product description within prepare the outline business case. The project brief is assembled later and draws that definition together with the rest of the starting point, while the breakdown structure and project plan belong to initiating a project.

stem: Who identifies, selects and appoints the project management team?
answer: The project executive, in consultation with the senior user and the project manager
distractors: The project manager, having designed the team structure, and the role descriptions
The business layer, in consultation with the project executive and the sponsor
The project board as a whole, at its first meeting, and by unanimous agreement
The senior supplier for supplier roles, and the executive for the rest
The programme manager, where a programme exists, and the project manager
The project executive acting alone, without consulting the senior user or the manager
explanation: The executive appoints the team in consultation with the senior user and project manager, while the manager designs the structure and prepares role descriptions. The RACI chart keeps the executive accountable for the activity and the manager responsible.

stem: The project manager has designed the team structure and drafted the role descriptions. What does the method say about accountability for the resulting appointments?
answer: The executive remains the single point of accountability for appointing the team, though the manager did the design
distractors: The manager becomes accountable because they designed the structure, and the executive only approves it
Accountability is shared between the executive and the manager, who both sign the appointments
Accountability passes to the business layer, which appointed the executive
The board assumes accountability once it approves the role descriptions, and the executive is relieved
Accountability sits with whoever signs the role descriptions, whether the manager or executive
Accountability is delegated to project support, which maintains the descriptions
explanation: Designing the structure and descriptions is the manager's work, but appointing the team is the executive's, and the RACI chart keeps accountability with the executive. Dividing the tasks does not divide accountability.

stem: Which question must the project approach settle before the project can be planned?
answer: Whether to build in-house or contract out
distractors: Which individuals will be appointed to the project board
What tolerances the board will set for each delivery stage
Which lessons from previous projects will be applied
When the initiation stage will end
How many work packages each team manager will receive
What quality criteria apply to each product
explanation: The delivery model, in-house or contracted, is one of the questions the project approach must answer before planning. The others concern modification versus build from scratch, COTS versus custom design, delivery methods and sustainability expectations.

stem: Why are user or supplier standards, practices and guidelines captured in the project brief as part of the project approach?
answer: Because they shape the management approaches created in initiating and must be understood by user and supplier
distractors: Because the brief must list every standard the supplier is contractually bound to, and the user's standards
Because they remove the need for a quality management approach, and for any further standards document
Because the board cannot approve the brief without them, and the executive must sign them off first
Because they determine the tolerances for the initiation stage, and for each delivery stage after it
Because they are required content of the outline business case, and the board reviews them each stage
Because they must be baselined before the mandate can be accepted, and the board has approved them
explanation: The manual says these standards influence the management approaches to be created in initiating a project, and capturing them ensures the approach is understood between user and supplier so the project is not jeopardized. They belong in the brief, not in the business case or the stage plan.

stem: When assembling the project brief, which of these must the project manager confirm?
answer: The project scope, its exclusions and the project tolerances
distractors: The stage tolerances for every delivery stage and its plan
The quality criteria for each product, and the reviewers
The business's risk appetite and the risk budget
The composition of each work package, and its team manager
The change authority for the project, and its budget limits
The benefits management approach and its review points
explanation: Assembling the brief covers current status, objectives and outcomes, scope with exclusions and project tolerances, constraints and assumptions, users and interested parties, roles and dependencies. Stage tolerances belong in the stage plan, and product-level quality criteria in product descriptions.

stem: While assembling the project brief, why does the project manager review the team structure and role descriptions?
answer: To identify any additional roles or skills needed in the ecosystem and prepare further role descriptions
distractors: To confirm the appointments already made by the project executive, and the roles they fill
To check that every role has a named deputy, and a person to cover absences
To decide which roles report directly to the project board, and which report to the project manager
To replace the role descriptions with a responsibility assignment matrix, and file them with the brief
To verify that the team can work within the initiation stage budget, and within the time available
To identify which team members can be released after initiation, and which must stay for delivery
explanation: The review tests completeness of the project ecosystem: additional roles or skills may be needed, and further descriptions are prepared as necessary. Confirming appointments is not the purpose, because the brief is about a commonly understood and well-defined starting point.

stem: Why does the process produce a stage plan for the initiation stage?
answer: Because initiation consumes time and resources, so the work should be planned and approved
distractors: Because the board needs a plan for the first delivery stage, and the brief, before approving it
Because the project plan, which the board needs, cannot be produced until the initiation stage is planned
Because the stage plan replaces the project brief as the basis for the initiation decision
Because the programme requires a stage plan for every project stage
Because it establishes the tolerances that the board will delegate, and the manager will apply
Because it records the benefits and dis-benefits for later comparison, and for the board's review
explanation: The stage plan exists to get initiation authorized and controlled, not to plan delivery; the project plan is created during initiating a project. In a programme, the stage end date is checked against the programme's plans, which also gives the programme early warning of its requirements.

stem: PRINCE2 notes that the project may choose to apply which other processes during the initiation stage?
answer: Controlling a stage and managing product delivery
distractors: Directing a project and closing a project
Managing a stage boundary and closing a project
Starting up a project and directing a project
Initiating a project and managing a stage boundary
Controlling a stage and managing a stage boundary
Managing product delivery and closing a project
explanation: Because initiation is real work that needs controlling, the project may apply controlling a stage and managing product delivery while initiating a project; deciding this is part of planning the initiation stage. Closing a project and managing a stage boundary fall at later points in the lifecycle.

stem: How does the process of starting up a project end?
answer: The project manager contacts the project board to request project initiation
distractors: The project executive submits the outline business case to the business layer
The project board issues the project mandate to the project manager
The programme manager authorizes the project manager to begin initiation
Project assurance recommends the brief to the executive for approval
The project manager issues the project initiation documentation to the board
The senior user signs off the project product description
explanation: The last activity is a request to the board supported by the outline business case and project brief, and it triggers directing a project. The project initiation documentation is produced later, during initiating a project.

stem: What is the purpose of the formal request made at the end of the process?
answer: To secure authority, people and resources for the initiation stage from the project board
distractors: To obtain approval of the project plan and the full business case
To hand the project over to the delivery teams, and close the process, after approval
To confirm that the project's benefits have been justified to the business
To authorize the project manager to commit the whole project budget
To close starting up a project and begin delivery, and record the decision
To record the board's acceptance of the project's risks, and the actions to take
explanation: The manager briefs the board on the outline business case, project product, approach, appointments and the initiation stage's activities and controls, then formally asks for authority so people and resources can be secured. Approving the project plan and business case happens at the end of initiating a project.

stem: The activities are combined and run concurrently on a small project. What must be preserved?
answer: The integrity of the link to directing a project at the request to initiate
distractors: The sequence of the seven activities exactly as listed in the manual, with no overlap at all
A separate approval of each management product by the project board, before the brief is assembled
The appointment of a team manager before the brief is assembled
The creation of a lessons log regardless of whether lessons exist
The production of the daily log before the mandate is reviewed
A stage plan for every stage identified in the project approach
explanation: Activities may be combined, split or run concurrently to suit the context, but the link to directing a project at the point of the initiation request must stay sound. The method does not require the listed sequence to be followed rigidly, nor board approval of each product.

stem: A project manager is not appointed until late in the process. What does PRINCE2 allow?
answer: The executive or anyone they appoint may create the products, provided single accountability is kept
distractors: The process must be restarted once the manager is appointed, and every product recreated from scratch
The board must approve each product created before the appointment, and the manager must then ratify it
The products may be created by the business layer and later ratified by the manager
The manager must recreate any product they did not personally produce, and sign each one as their own
The executive becomes accountable for the products and cannot delegate the work, even to a deputy
The process is suspended until a manager is in place, and the board is informed of the delay
explanation: Appointing the manager early is good practice, but if it happens later the executive or their nominee can create the products, just as the executive need not write the outline business case personally. What must survive is a single point of accountability for each role's duty.

stem: According to the RACI chart for the process, who is accountable for the appointment of the project executive and the project manager?
answer: The business layer, which also appoints the executive
distractors: The project executive, who is accountable for every other activity in the process
The project board, acting collectively
The project manager, on the board's behalf
The programme manager, where a programme exists
The senior user, representing the business interest
Project assurance, which checks the appointment
explanation: The chart marks this activity A/R for the business layer, with the executive also responsible: the business is accountable for the appointments and responsible for appointing the executive. For the remaining activities the executive is accountable.

stem: How does the quality practice apply to the process of starting up a project?
answer: Users' quality expectations and any known specifications or standards are captured in the project product description
distractors: Quality criteria for every product are agreed with the board before initiation, and then baselined at once
The quality register is created and baselined during the process
Product descriptions are written for each product in the initiation stage plan, and approved by the board before the stage starts
Quality tolerances are set for the project and recorded in the project mandate
Acceptance criteria are tested against the project product before the brief is assembled
The quality management approach is approved by the board alongside the brief, and then issued to teams
explanation: Quality expectations and known standards are recorded in the project product description and refined during initiating a project and stage planning through individual product descriptions. The quality management approach, the quality register and product descriptions are created later.

stem: How does the progress practice apply to the process of starting up a project?
answer: Known project tolerances go into the brief, while initiation stage tolerances go into its stage plan
distractors: All tolerances are deferred until the project plan is created during initiation
Project tolerances are agreed by the board only after initiation is authorized
Stage tolerances for delivery are set now and recorded in the project brief
The initiation stage has no tolerances because it is authorized by a single request
Tolerances are recorded in the daily log until the project plan exists
The board delegates tolerance to the executive rather than to the project manager
explanation: Known project tolerances are identified and included in the brief, to be refined and approved after the process, while initiation stage tolerances are identified in the stage plan for approval. Neither is deferred entirely, and delivery stage tolerances are not set at this point.
